(1) MAHC (mahc_hierarchical on): each pipeline that returned an in-scope list votes with weight w = max(pi, 1e-4) / (sigma^2 + 1e-4), normalised (sigma None counts as 1; skipped, failed and abstained pipelines do not vote); weighted Borda, rank r of n scores (n - r + 1)/n, ties by name; fused sigma = sqrt(sum w sigma^2). (2) Priors pi (M-a): a pipeline's top-3 hit rate on build cases with the same trigger signal type, smoothed toward its global rate with 10 pseudo-cases, used only with at least 30 build cases where the pipeline gave a list, else the global rate; a pipeline never seen weighs 1. Signal type: for the trigger's top suspect, its metric series with the largest causal z at the trigger bucket, classified by name: error (error, fail, 5xx), then latency (latency, duration, response_time), then resource (cpu, mem, memory, gc, thread, fd, disk, socket), else unclassified; z ties (z is capped at 50) go to the reverse-alphabetically larger name; the series need not have crossed (a log-driven trigger is typed by the suspect's strongest metric series); a fallback trigger or a window without metrics is unclassified; the detector is unchanged. The modality level is dropped. (3) Calibrated confidence (M-b, replaces Ch3's entropy floor): features of the fused result (top-1 share, entropy / log n, fused sigma, contributing pipelines, top-1s agree) -> logistic score of standardised features (L2 strength 1) -> isotonic regression to P(root in fused top 3): equal scores pooled first, then pool-adjacent-violators, knots on the score computed from the stored (rounded) parameters; a score maps to the value of the last knot at or below it (the first knot's value below the range). (4) Fitting: nested cross-fitting on outer folds = OTel by root service, RCAEval by system; within a training set each case's features come from priors fitted without its group; no case is scored by priors or a calibrator that saw its group. The frozen parameters are refitted on all build cases (priors on all; calibrator on group-held-out features). (5) Floor (M-c, M-e): per corpus the lowest held-out confidence c with HR@3 >= 0.8 among cases with confidence >= c; the floor is the stricter corpus's; if a corpus has no such c the build run stops and is brought to the owner (no automatic fallback). CONFIRMED when every pipeline is in and confidence >= floor, else PROVISIONAL + human request. (6) Timing: pipeline latencies replayed as if concurrent, except that G-pipe starts after D-pipe's routing gate (its finish time is D-pipe's latency plus its own): first publication at the earlier of 30 s and all pipelines done, from those done; terminal when all are done within 90 s; otherwise non-converged (PROVISIONAL + human request, fused from pipelines done by 90 s). The scored list is the terminal one; TTT = first publication of any state (the contract's "first PROVISIONAL" read as first publication, since variants with no gate never publish a PROVISIONAL); timing fields are outside rerun equality and reported as measured on the stated hardware, except at the 90 s cutoff: a pipeline that finishes after 90 s on one run and before it on another changes the state (NON_CONVERGED) and drops that pipeline from the scored list; non_converged is stored per run and reported. change: Engine and narrators: the Narrative Engine (helios/narrative/, gated by VCLFlag.COE_NARRATIVE; HELIOS-noExpl shows the ranked list only) writes one narrative per stored run from that run's CoE entry alone. A narrative is a code-filled header (fused top 3, confidence, state) and three slots: story, contradictions, verification. The narrator is chosen by l2c_llm: off (HELIOS-noLLM, -D, -G), a deterministic template narrator that never calls a model (N-a); on, an LLM narrator on the frozen llama3.1:8b (digest 46e0c10c039e) through L-pipe's gateway and response cache, one call per slot. Both emit typed claims (ranking, shift, call_structure, log_message, contradiction, verification_step) that cite CoE IDs. L-pipe worker claims are not citable. Kind rules: a deterministic verifier accepts a claim only if every cite exists and the kind's rule holds: a shift needs the claim's own D-pipe channel item, with its direction taken from the cited before/after levels; a call_structure claim needs the caller → callee edge in the cited G-pipe item; a log snippet must be at least 12 characters, a whole-word run of the cited line, quoted once in the sentence; a ranking claim must match the fused ranking; a contradiction's pipeline must be in the disagree list; a verification step's target must be in the fused top 3 or a cited caller/callee, with a read-only verb first, a modality matching the cited item and at least one cite. Closed vocabulary: the sentence must also be contained under a closed vocabulary (owner decision N-j, taken after the whole-branch review showed that containment alone let negations, invented causes and reversed edges through): one line, at most 40 words, with no brackets, no quotes outside the snippet and no citation IDs; only the claim's own service names, and every other word from the frozen word list of its kind (the list contains no negations, causes or mutating verbs); the rank word, channel words, direction words, caller-before-callee order and pipeline name agree with the claim's fields; every number is a plain number matched to the claim's own evidence in its own unit: percent only for fractions, s/ms only for ms items, the before value before the after value, within ±1% or the stated precision; wall-clock times only in verification steps, as HH:MM inside the capture window, also across midnight (N-b, N-c, N-f, N-g, N-j). Rejection reasons are a closed set of 16 (design §5.5 plus word_not_allowed and malformed_sentence). Retry and fallback: a slot with any rejection gets one retry at the pinned temperature, carrying the rejected answer and the reasons; after that it gets the template's slot, logged as a fallback. A model error never fails a run (N-d). Storage: the narrative is stored in narrative_row and as step N of the signed CoE entry: claims, attempts, rejections, first-draft counts and rendered text, with tokens under cost and wall time under measured. Narrator tokens count in CpR (incident_usage); narrator time is outside TTT. Additive CoE fields: D-pipe items carry raw before/after levels with units (N-i): OTel latency in ms, errors per step, otherwise the metric name. Ranking, mu, sigma and the decision hash are unchanged. The T step carries window_start and window_end. Frozen parameters: data/frozen/narrator_params.json holds the direction words and the verbs (query, inspect, verify, check, filter); the per-kind vocabulary, plus the channel, rank and pipeline words; the tolerance, max 3 steps, the 40-word limit and the 12-character snippet minimum. Its hash (narrator_params) and, for LLM variants, the prompt SHA (narrator_prompt) are written into each CoE entry's parameter_hashes. The prompt lists the slot's allowed words. Confirmatory runs refuse a provisional narrator (the prompt for LLM variants, the parameters for all narrating variants) until the prompt round is chosen and frozen in entry C. Machine report: helios/evaluation/narrative_report.py gives per narrator: first-pass acceptance, rejections by reason, retry success, slot fallback rate, and sentence and slot shapes by source (N-h). change: Computational rules of the analysis suite (helios/analysis/, bin/analyse.py, analysis-v1); no hypothesis, comparison, metric, direction, alpha or rank changes. (1) Holm (T-a): standard step-down in the order of the observed p-values; the k-th smallest of the eight is compared with 0.05 / (9 - k); ties go by registered rank; the registered rank sets the report order and the alpha column reads "threshold if tested k-th". An untestable hypothesis has no p-value, sorts last, is not rejected and stays in the family. The fixed-sequence reading (registered rank order, stop at the first failure) is reported beside it as a sensitivity row. Holm-adjusted p-values are reported. (2) Wilcoxon signed-rank (T-b): differences a - b in the registered direction, one-sided; zeros dropped; ties get midranks; the p-value is the exact conditional distribution of T+ given the observed midranks (enumerated over all sign patterns). With no non-zero difference the hypothesis is tested and not rejected. On 0/1 outcomes (HR@3: A-H1, A-H2, A-H3, A-H4, A-H6, A-H8) this equals the exact sign test on discordant pairs; reported beside each such test. (3) A-H7 (T-c): one exact one-sided sign test on H_fact (rater labels) and one on H_struct, each on the per-case sign of Full - noLLM with zeros dropped; A-H7 is rejected only when both are (intersection-union test), and its p-value is the larger of the two. Cases with pending labels leave the H_fact pair (entry 84). (4) A-H5 (T-d): the primary test uses the cases where both variants have the same HR@3 outcome, with the matched share reported; all cases as the registered sensitivity; descriptive splits by the Full run's stage (stopped, escalated; entry 69); log-CpR without the opportunity component only as an exploratory column. (5) McNemar exact mid-p (T-e): b = Full hits and the baseline misses, c = the reverse; mid-p = P(X > b) + P(X = b) / 2 with X ~ Binomial(b + c, 1/2), in exact rational arithmetic; with b + c = 0, tested and not rejected. (6) Effect sizes (T-f): BCa interval (95 %) of the mean paired difference of the primary metric, 10,000 case resamples, seed bca_seed(hypothesis id); a degenerate set (all differences equal) gives the estimate with no interval and the reason. Cliff's delta over all cross pairs (ignores pairing; stated). Hodges-Lehmann = median of the Walsh averages. Cohen's h for HR@3 proportions. (7) Sensitivity (T-g): group-level exact Wilcoxon on per-group mean differences (groups = system x root-cause service x fault from the signed ground truth); rank-based mixed model on pooled ranks of both variants with a random intercept per group (statsmodels MixedLM, REML), one-sided p of the variant coefficient, ICC = group / (group + residual variance); Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 per family; paired t on log values for B-H6 and B-H7, and on raw Avg@5 for B-H8. analytic_consequence: Decides which runs count, how a hypothesis is narrowed when one benchmark system's cell fails, and how missing data is reported. Under the cell rule a hypothesis may be tested on one benchmark system only, which lowers its power; the asymmetric rule then reports a non-rejection as inconclusive at delivered power. MCAR and IPW are sensitivity results and cannot change a binding result. The OTel build v3 campaign reproduced the S4.11 build run's eval_score rows exactly (1,596 rows). The analysis plan, metric contract, variant hashes and seed register are unchanged. No confirmatory data exists. The rules go into the OSF addendum deposit with entries 46 to 86 (S2-BL-05).
change: Rules of the run campaign (helios/orchestrator/schedule.py, campaign.py, helios/evaluation/cells.py, helios/analysis/missing.py, bin/helios_campaign.py, schedule-v1); no hypothesis, variant, metric, test, direction, alpha or seed register changes. (1) Schedule (O-a): one frozen schedule per corpus, a pure function of the sealed manifest's case_order, the case-to-system map and the variant catalogue, with a SHA-256 digest recorded in every run's context; phases confirmatory (8 x 240), baselines (5 x 240), exploratory (consumed Tier-2 variants x 240), scoring and cells, determinism rerun, E-H5 replay; run ids derived from the digest, spec and attempt; the registered run_seed recorded per run. (2) Order (O-b): case by case in case_order; inside a case HELIOS-noRouter first, then Ch3 Table 17 order, so the run that fills the response cache, and the wall times later variants replay, is the same variant on every case; the order is logged. (3) Outcomes (O-c): passed and excluded as the integrity gate decides; a capture hash or seal failure is an exclusion with an exclusion-ledger entry (before: reconciliation "skipped" only); an infrastructure error (model server unreachable or timed out, connection, timeout, out of memory), decided by exception class and never by the result, is retried at most twice and then excluded; any other run error is excluded and the campaign continues; configuration refusals (provisional parameters, missing signing key, router or model mismatch, external trigger, pool lock) stop the campaign and are not exclusions; every result-store write of a run is one transaction, and an unfinished run is discarded and re-run under its next attempt number. After scoring, a passed run without a value for a cell metric is excluded for that metric only (H_fact only once its labels are due; a censored TTCD and HR@k of an empty list are values). (4) Exclusion entries (O-d): the seven required fields plus signed campaign context (phase, corpus, system, seed, attempt, schedule digest, metric) and label-free run covariates; ground truth is never written by the run path. The repo-root exclusion ledger is the pool campaign's; every other campaign writes its own anchored ledger. (5) Cells (O-e): a cell is system x benchmark system x metric, its share the cases with a value over the cases the schedule gave it, entering inference at a share of at least 4/5; a hypothesis is tested on the cases of the benchmark systems where both compared cells pass, and is untestable (counted, never dropped) when none passes. This replaces the interim per-hypothesis rule of entry 86 item 9. (6) MCAR and IPW (O-f), sensitivity only, per hypothesis over its scheduled case pairs (a pair is missing when either run is excluded or its cell fails): with at least 10 missing and 10 complete pairs, a logistic regression of "pair missing" on benchmark system, fault type and window bytes with a likelihood-ratio test against the intercept-only model; otherwise, or when the model does not converge, descriptive per-covariate counts with Fisher's exact test for two-level covariates and the exact rank-sum test for continuous ones (asymptotic when tied, stated); with no missing pair, not applicable. IPW: the same model for "pair complete", stabilised weights truncated at the 1st and 99th percentiles, the weighted mean paired difference with a weighted BCa interval (paired resampling, bca_seed of the hypothesis); no weighted p-value. (7) Subsets (O-g): the determinism rerun takes every 10th case of each benchmark system in case_order, runs every scheduled HELIOS variant that calls the model with the cache bypassed into a separate store, and compares the fused list, the narrative and the L-pipe evidence; a non-equal run is flagged nondeterministic. The E-H5 delayed-label subset is every 4th case of each benchmark system of the pool case_order (25 %). Both use the opaque-ID order, which is drawn from the seed register, so no new seed block is used. (8) Exploratory variants whose changed flag has no reader outside helios/vcl are refused from the schedule with the reason recorded (today HELIOS-noCogni, HIS3, noFGSV, noIOL); a confirmatory variant is never refused.
